claims.text: The initial Mo-Nb-Ta-W alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase refractory HEA with no prior precipitate formation.
Untreated homogeneous Mo-Nb-Ta-W typically exhibits brittle or uneven deformation under dynamic conditions.
Annealing Mo-Nb-Ta-W at approximately 900°C for 1 hour followed by rapid quenching will induce nanoprecipitate formation.
The induced nanoprecipitates will be uniformly distributed and coherent with the HEA matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitates will obstruct dislocation motion and thereby maintain high strength.
The nanoprecipitates will act as nucleation sites that promote sustained dislocation accumulation.
Sustained dislocation accumulation will enhance strain hardening.
Enhanced strain hardening will improve ductility and uniform deformability.
Precise control of precipitate size and distribution will prevent degradation of the alloy's impact-induced energetic response.
The heat-treated alloy will have significantly greater ductility than the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will deform more uniformly under mechanical testing than the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will preserve the high yield strength of the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will preserve impact-induced energy release relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed benefits depend on maintaining precipitate coherence and avoiding excessive coarsening.
Overheating or excessively slow quenching could cause deleterious precipitate growth or loss of coherence.
Precipitate growth or loss of coherence would undermine the balance between ductility and strength.
